title: Static prerendering vs rendering per request

slides.text: Build the HTML once, ahead of time 🏗️
slides.say: Not every page needs to render on each request. Some can be generated once, ahead of time. That's static site generation.
Pre render, from react dom static, renders your app to static HTML. You get a prelude stream back. On the client, you still hydrate it.

slides.text: prerender waits for ALL Suspense boundaries to resolve. Data loaded with Suspense ends up in the HTML.
slides.say: The key difference: pre render waits for every Suspense boundary to resolve. So data loaded with Suspense ends up inside the HTML.

slides.text: Streaming SSR shows content as it loads, per request. prerender doesn't stream: it's for generating pages ahead of time.
slides.say: Streaming server rendering reveals content as it loads, on every request. Pre render doesn't stream. It's made for generating pages ahead of time.
With web streams, use pre render. On Node, use pre render to node stream.
